### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 42 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `77177f57e776489a4054d9d49abfb1c839986dce` — the merge of head `efa6f7562b47929d3db32480a809d5e83ac794d4` into base `da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 77177f57e776489a4054d9d49abfb1c839986dce && git checkout 77177f57e776489a4054d9d49abfb1c839986dce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165 efa6f7562b47929d3db32480a809d5e83ac794d4 && git checkout -B drift-repro da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165 && git merge --no-ff efa6f7562b47929d3db32480a809d5e83ac794d4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c4f1e6c201eec5e58b971a0d7fbcbf9ca1579d60`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dotted-path-preview-parity.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dotted-dimension-unbacked-join-parity.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-refusal-envelope.test.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts (`unbackedRelationshipPath`, `compileDataset`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/hop-object.ts (`resolvePathHops`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-refusal.ts (`invalidMemberError`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts (the filter fold), packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts (`getObjectFieldNames`, `relationshipResolver`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts (time-dimension resolution), packages/objectql/src/declared-read-columns.ts (`PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS`), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts (the one `DATASET_INVALID` reader), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx, docs/adr/0037-live-canvas-draft-preview.md. The changeset is the prose face and is not reviewed. Read on `origin/main` `f5a400afd` (no commit since the merge base `0b6a52e8a` touches `service-analytics` or the rest test) and on the head's tree.

Inputs: cards #28555–#28558 (bodies, triage records, claims, the os-dev-report `6558864662`), the family precedent (#28258: triage `6532297703`, claim `6553559505`, dev report `6554100004`, merged PR #28553 and its changeset), PR #28686's body, file list and net diff, and the head's check-runs. Judged on the tree, not on the body's account of it.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, read in the head's `analytics-service.ts` against the live helpers:

1. **Draft preview refuses any member read through a relationship path** (`assertPreviewJoinsNothing`, last in the preview gate list, `relationshipMembers(q, cube, true)`: `dimensions`, `timeDimensions`, `measures`, the lowered `where` leaves). `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 via `invalidMemberError` with `member`, `param`, `cube`. Before: one `null` group, `[]`, or a total of `0` (measured by the #28258 dev at `eeec88d14`, re-measured by this dev at `0b6a52e8`). **Right.** It is a narrowing of the preview face only; the two live strategies are untouched for a backed path (the gate is asked only inside the `previewDrafts` branch). The base lookup column itself (`account`) is a bare identifier and is not in `relationshipMembers`, so it still groups (pinned as a CONTROL).
2. **`OBJECT.region` / `CUBE.region` now answer live groups in the preview** (`previewEvaluationCube` hands the evaluator an alias entry under the spelling; every gate still reads the plain cube). `declaredMemberEntry` resolves those spellings to the declared `region` (tail / flat lookup, the strategies' `lookupMember` mirror), so they never enter `relationshipMembers`. **Right**, and it is a widening of the preview's answer set only in the sense that a request that was served a wrong `null` group is now served the right groups; no new code, status, member or export. It stays inside `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` because nothing that was refused is now served.
3. **Undeclared dotted `timeDimensions` entry and `where` leaf refused on every face** by the one gate (`assertDimensionJoinsBacked` now iterates `relationshipMembers(query, cube, false)`; `declared` entries skipped; `unbackedRelationshipPath(column, allowed)` is the single judgement of "is this path backed", PR #28553's helper, unchanged in `dataset-compiler.ts`). The `dimensions` message is byte-unchanged; the noun table adds `Time dimension` and `Filter member`. Native moves `DATASET_INVALID` to `INVALID_FIELD` for a `runtimeFilter` member and a windowed-only time dimension through an undeclared path. **Right**, and the seat ruling on #28258 (claim `6553559505`: "`INVALID_FIELD` / 400 naming the member on all three faces") and #28557's triage direction are what this implements. The `where` leaves are read through `normalizeAnalyticsFilterTree` + `collectFilterLeaves` with `NO_DATETIME_COLUMNS`, the same lowering `namedQueryFields` and `assertWhereFields` read, with the same stand-down on a tree the normalizer refuses (it is refused where it already is, `INVALID_FILTER`). A nested-relation spelling (`{ account: { name: … } }`) names the member `account` (bare) and is not judged here, as before.
4. **`DATASET_INVALID` stays for every other reason it is raised.** Verified in the tree: `dataset-compiler.ts` (`assertDeclared`, hop limit, unknown relationship, aggregate and duration refusals), `dataset-executor.ts` and the native allowlist's hook for a hand-authored cube (`allowed` undefined ⇒ both new gates return) are untouched; the allowlist code in `native-sql-strategy.ts` changes a comment only. The rest route's envelope branch (`analytics-routes.ts`) classifies on `code` + 4xx `status`, so the moved code reaches the HTTP caller as `400 INVALID_FIELD` with the message intact; the diff's rest row pins exactly that at the REST door.
5. **Backed path to a column the related object lacks refused before SQL on every face** (`assertRelationshipColumnsExist`, called right after the join gate in `callCtx` and at the same point in the preview; skips any member whose path is unbacked; resolves the last hop with `resolvePathHops(cube, baseObject, hops, this.hopReference)`, the resolver the admission and both strategies read, tier 1 the compiled `joins`, tier 2 the declared `reference`; column judged against `getObjectFieldNames(object)` plus `id` / `created_at` / `updated_at`). **Right**, and no valid dataset is newly refused by it: `getObjectFieldNames` is `Object.keys(engine.getObject(name).fields)` (plugin.ts), which carries every declared field of every kind (formula, lookup, virtual, and the system fields `applySystemFields` writes into the map), and the admitted triple is `PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS`, the data door's own; the gate stands down (no refusal) when the probe is absent, the object is unknown to it (an external datasource, or a join target named by table rather than object), or the cube's `sql` is not a bare object name, exactly as the base-object gates do. `hops` is never empty (the column matched `IDENTIFIER_PATH`), so `hops[hops.length - 1]` cannot throw. Native `DATABASE_ERROR` / 500 for this case becomes `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 with `field` and `object`; ObjectQL's own 400 for it is pre-empted by the same message, so the three faces answer alike (pinned on both the dimension and the `runtimeFilter` position).
6. **Order of verdicts holds.** Both new gates sit after `assertFieldsReadable` in `callCtx` and after it in the preview's gate list, so #20933's 403 for a path through an unreadable object still comes first; `assertPreviewJoinsNothing` is after the two live-parity gates, so an unbacked path and a missing related column keep the live faces' one message on the preview and only a path the live strategies would serve reaches the preview-only refusal. The #28258 dev's noted preview residual (an undeclared path through an unreadable object answers 400 before the object's 403 on the preview, because the preview admits only `cubeObjects`) is unchanged and not this PR's.
7. **Readers of `DATASET_INVALID` for the two moved native cases**, measured by me on `origin/main` with `git grep` across the tree (`ui/` included) and in the `objectui` checkout: outside `service-analytics` the code is read at runtime only by `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` branch ⑤, which treats every self-named non-permission code alike (`throw new Error('Dataset query failed: …')`); the two ui tests use it as fixture text; `packages/rest`'s envelope tests pin the envelope, not this producer (and the one row that did is moved in this diff); `packages/client`, `packages/cli`, `packages/runtime`, `apps/` and dogfood read it nowhere; the spec ledger lists the code generically for `@objectstack/service-analytics` and pins it to no selection-side condition. The dev's measurement is confirmed: no real consumer, so both halves land and no decision card is owed.
8. **Comment-only edits** to `native-sql-strategy.ts` (allowlist docblock) and `preview-evaluator.ts` (header): the header's "joins via `include` fall back to the caller's normal execution path" was never true in the tree (measured `null` group) and is replaced with the refusal; right, see ④.
9. **Tests**: the new 15-case file drives all three faces through `queryDataset` on real SQLite; `refusedAlike` pins code, status, `param`, `member`, `cube` and byte-equal messages across faces; CONTROLs pin that native still serves the backed `runtimeFilter` member and the windowed time dimension and that the base lookup column groups on every face. The #28258 file's backed-path CONTROL now pins the preview's own refusal and that its message is not the unbacked one. The rest row pins the moved code at the REST door with the message regex.

**Check-runs on `c4f1e6c2`** at read time (2026-11-01T13:53Z, 45 runs): `success` on Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, filter; `skipped` on the UI / docs / opt-in / temporal families (path-filtered, nothing of theirs is touched); **`in_progress` on Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Lint ESLint / CI / docs / repo / scoped ×2, Type Check ×4 and Live E2E UI**. An in-progress check is not a verdict: the derived test, lint and type families are not concluded at this read, and the seat lands only on their success. The dev's local run of the 62 derived families (all exit 0, incl. `check:error-status-conformance` and `check:changeset-no-major`) and the full dogfood battery on this head are the body's account, not a gate verdict.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28555-dotted-path-preview-parity.md`: `'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` present and identical on the PR body and the changeset; title `fix(service-analytics)!:` with a **BREAKING** paragraph. **Matches.** Under the repo's level axis (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: the level follows the metadata protocol alone; `Metadata-protocol: none` must grade every introduced entry `patch`) a narrowing with no protocol change is `patch`, and PR #28553 (the family precedent, merged) carried the identical shape. The diff publishes no export, type, schema key, code or status; the only package moved is `service-analytics`; no `authorable-surface` baseline moves. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. The `Clause-②` line names the three narrowings (preview path members; undeclared path in `timeDimensions` / `runtimeFilter` on every face with the native code move; backed path to a missing column before SQL) and the one non-narrowing (`OBJECT.region` answered), which is what the tree does.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared; none found owed.
- **Dev flag: "which way #28555 went" (refuse, not join).** The order's alternatives were the seat's to allow; judged in ④: refusing is the right design on this tree.
- **Dev flag: `DATASET_INVALID` readers measured, `ui/` included.** Re-measured by me (① item 7): confirmed, no consumer branches on the code; no decision card owed under #28257's triage condition.
- **Dev flag: `Skills-docs: none`.** Read: no file under `skills/**` or `content/docs` says the draft preview joins, and `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx` ("Only declared paths are joinable") is a statement this PR makes true of time dimensions and filter members too. The `previewDrafts` mentions in docs are the meta-read overlay (ADR-0033) and ADR-0037, not the dataset preview's join behaviour. Accepted.
- **Dev flag: three out-of-scope findings.** Each is outside this PR's four cards: (1) the preview drops a bucketed plain `closed_at` time dimension not also in `dimensions` (no relationship path; a preview-evaluator grouping defect); (2) a `runtimeFilter` member spelled `OBJECT.region` answers `[]` on the preview (the where-tree spelling, which #28555's reach names only for dimensions; a second walker, correctly not added here); (3) ObjectQL answers a backed `account.id` dimension `INVALID_QUERY` about a duplicate groupBy (a live ObjectQL face defect the cards do not name; this PR leaves the live faces as they are). All three are class (a), measured, and belong on new cards; none is a gap the cards' Wanted lines cover.
- **Seat constraints:** `packages/spec/**` and `ui/**` untouched (file list); PR has no assignees or labels beyond the auto-labeller's; one branch, one PR for the four cards, `Fixes` ×4 (closing-keyword parity gate success).
- **Escalated: nothing.**

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the cited code:

**Does refusing a BACKED relationship-path member in the preview take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The published spec declares that joins are derived from `include` and only declared paths are joinable (`analytics.mdx`), and that the Studio dataset preview runs on the same governed path as widgets and reports. The draft preview under `previewDrafts` is a different thing: ADR-0037 chose B-min, an in-memory overlay of the base object's pending seed rows, "the smallest honest mechanism", with acceptance "the drafted dashboard charts real numbers from the drafted seed". Nothing in the spec, the ADR, the docs or `packages/spec` says the seed overlay joins a related object, and the tree never did: `evaluateAnalyticsQueryOverRows` reads `cube.dimensions[name].sql` as a row key of the base object's seed rows, so a backed `account.name` was a key that no row carried, and the answer was one `null` group holding the whole total, `[]` for a filter, `0` for a windowed time dimension. That is a silent wrong answer, not a delivered capability. The one declaration pointing the other way was the evaluator header's "falls back to the caller's normal execution path", a code comment, never implemented, and not an honest fallback for a draft object either (the live table does not hold the seed, so a fallback would chart the published world, the #19810 case: "a fall-back only where a fall-back exists"). The PR retires that claim where it stood and makes the refusal real; it does not narrow a capability a consumer had. The card's own Wanted allows "or refuses it with the live refusal; never a silent null group": the live faces have no refusal for a backed path, so the dev chose the family's member-level envelope (`INVALID_FIELD` / 400, `member`, `param`, `cube`) with a message that names the member, the path and the two remedies; the same code and shape the preview-parity family converged on (#28172, #28201, #28257, #28258). Joining in the preview would have meant reading the related object's rows from its own seed and/or table with two different keys, under an admission and scope the preview branch does not apply to related objects (`cubeObjects` admits the base and declared joins; seed rows take no read scope): a second query engine, as the dev says. Refusing is right on this tree.

**One judgement of "backed".** Yes: `unbackedRelationshipPath` (PR #28553) is the only test, asked by `assertDimensionJoinsBacked` (refuse when non-null) and by `assertRelationshipColumnsExist` (skip when non-null); `assertPreviewJoinsNothing` asks nothing about backing, because it runs after both and refuses whatever remains. `relationshipMembers` resolves every position through `declaredMemberEntry`, the one `lookupMember` mirror, with the same `kind` per position as `namedQueryFields` (`timeDimensions` as `'any'`, which the strategies resolve as `'dimension'`; that difference is #20917's, pre-existing, and changes nothing on this PR's inputs).

**Tried to break it:**

- A dataset-declared dimension over a backed path (`account_name` over `account.name`): preview refuses with `param: 'dimensions'`, `member: 'account_name'`; live serves. Right.
- A dataset measure over a related field (`score_max` over `account.score`): preview refuses (`withMeasures: true`); live serves on native. Right.
- The dataset's own `filter` or a measure's `filter` over a related field: `DatasetExecutor` folds both into the `where` it hands the service (`combineFilters(compiled.filter, selection.runtimeFilter)`, then the measure filter), so the preview refuses every selection on such a dataset with `param: 'where'` and the dataset's member. Loud, where it served `[]`; see should-fix 3 for the attribution.
- `OBJECT.region` as a `runtimeFilter` member on the preview: not a relationship member (resolves to `region`), so not refused, and the evaluator matches the key as written: `[]`. Out-of-scope finding 2, correctly filed, not a regression.
- A multi-hop backed path (`account.owner.name`, both declared): `resolvePathHops` walks both via the compiled `joins`; the column is judged on the owner's object. Unbacked at the second hop: the join gate names `account.owner` first. Right.
- A related object the probe cannot see (external datasource, or a join target named by its table): the column gate stands down and the strategies answer as before. No new refusal.
- Hand-authored cube through `/analytics/query`: `allowed` undefined, both gates return; the native allowlist and `DATASET_INVALID` stay. Right.
- `where` an operator the normalizer refuses: `relationshipMembers` catches and names nothing; `INVALID_FILTER` where it already is. Right.
- A caller-minted measure (`mintCallerMeasures`) over a dotted spelling is refused at the mint before these gates. Unchanged.
- Refusal bodies at the REST door: the route's envelope branch reads `code` and a 4xx `status` first, and the diff's rest row drives the real service through the route and pins `400`, `code: INVALID_FIELD`, the message, and no `error` member. Consistent with the other member-level refusals.

**Findings:**

- **Should-fix 1 (same family as #28558, measure position, read not measured).** `assertRelationshipColumnsExist` is called with `withMeasures: false` on both sites, `assertMeasureFields` stands down on a dotted source, and `compileDataset`'s `assertAggregateFieldTypeCompatible` returns on a dotted `field`. So a dataset measure `{ aggregate: 'max', field: 'account.bogus' }` with `include: ['account']` is judged by no gate and, by the same reading that produced the card, still reaches SQL on the native strategy as `DATABASE_ERROR` / 500, while ObjectQL refuses it 400 and the preview now refuses it with the preview message. The card's reach was the dimension and the dev added the filter, so the card as filed is met; but the title names "a declared dotted path" and the measure position is the same defect one flag away. Either pass `true` for the column gate (measures resolve through `cube.measures`, the same `declaredMemberEntry` path, and the preview already reads them) with one pin, or file it as a class (a) finding with a measurement.
- **Should-fix 2 (test honesty, `packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-refusal-envelope.test.ts`).** The row whose `listEntry` is `not backed by a declared relationship` now triggers the service gate's `INVALID_FIELD`, and the row's own new comment says no request member reaches the native allowlist on this route any more. The `covers exactly the five entries #5367 deleted` pin is then held by the string alone: the allowlist producer (`datasetInvalidError` in `native-sql-strategy.ts`) is driven through the REST seam by nothing. The row is still worth keeping (it is now the one REST-door pin of the moved code), but its audit claim should say so plainly, and the file header's "five producers … five entries" count should note that one producer is reachable only by a hand-authored cube, outside this route. No behaviour hangs on it.
- **Should-fix 3 (message attribution on the preview).** When the refused `where` leaf comes from the dataset's own `filter` or a measure's `filter` (folded by the executor), the message says "Filter member 'account.name' … publish the draft … or preview without it", with `param: 'where'`, though the caller's request carries no such member and cannot preview without it. `assertWhereFields` (#28257) has the same attribution and was accepted, so this is not new; a clause naming the dataset's filter as the source when the member is absent from `selection.runtimeFilter` would make the remedy the right reader's. Wording only.
- No must-fix. The narrowing makes the spec's own rule (only declared paths are joinable; a preview that cannot answer refuses rather than answers wrong) real at every position and on every face, takes nothing away that was delivered or declared to a consumer, uses one judgement of backing, keeps `DATASET_INVALID` for every other reason, and moves no code with a reader that branches on it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `efa6f7562b47929d3db32480a809d5e83ac794d4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dotted-path-preview-parity.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-refusal-envelope.test.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts (`relationshipMembers`, `declaredMemberEntry`, `mintCallerMeasures`, the `callCtx` cube read), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts (`compileDataset`: measure `sql`, derived and duration sidecars, `assertAggregateFieldTypeCompatible`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-refusal.ts (`invalidMemberError`). No changeset or prose face moves in the delta.

Delta review. This record extends the base record on `c4f1e6c201eec5e58b971a0d7fbcbf9ca1579d60`, PR comment 6558997053, whose ①–④ judgments stand unless named here. The delta is one commit, `efa6f7562`, on that head: `git diff c4f1e6c2 efa6f756` touches three files (+34 / −8), nothing else.

### ① Derived judgments
